deep.reconstruction:
The heading 'Rechnung bei 60°' means 'calculation at 60°'. The page is a numerical evaluation of Gauss's lemniscatic entire functions P(φ) and Q(φ) at φ = ϖ/3. Here sl φ = P(φ)/Q(φ), and '60°' means one third of the half-period ϖ (ϖ/3 ↔ 60° when ϖ ↔ 180°). The aim is to test closed forms for P(ϖ/3) and Q(ϖ/3) after removing the factor e^{πψ²/2} with ψ = 1/3, i.e. e^{π/18}. These are evidently the analogues of the 90° case ψ = 1/2, which the next page treats ('90° … ⁴√2').

(A) P series. The first number is 0.874019185 = ϖ/3, where ϖ = 2.6220575… is the lemniscate constant. The page evaluates
P(φ) = φ − 2φ⁵/5! − 36φ⁹/9! + …
• Terms: 2φ⁵/120 = 0.008500678 and 36φ⁹/9! = 0.0000295 (identified by me from the numbers).
• This coefficient pattern is the Weierstrass σ-series for g2 = 4: σ = z − z⁵/60 − z⁹/10080 − …
• Middle column: 0.874019185 − 0.008500678 = 0.865518507, then − 0.000029513 gives P(ϖ/3) ≈ 0.865488994.
• Left column: scratch work containing a misplaced 0.000295132, later corrected.

(B) Q series. Q(φ) = 1 + 2φ⁴/4! − 4φ⁸/8! + c·φ¹²/12! + …
• Terms: 2φ⁴/24 = 0.048629815, giving 1.048629815; 4φ⁸/8! = 0.0000337847.
• The third term is +0.000000169. Gauss's c is not legible; the numbers imply c ≈ 400.
• The middle column first misplaces the second term as 0.000337847. The right column redoes it: 1.0485940(30) + 169 → Q(ϖ/3) = 1.048594199, which carries a slip (see errors).
• Check (mine): P/Q = 0.8253787 = sl(ϖ/3) = (2√3−3)^{1/4}. This follows from 1 + y = 2√(1−y) with y = sl⁴, since sl(2ϖ/3) = sl(ϖ/3).

(C) The Gaussian factor.
• (1/18)π·0.434 is (π/18)·log10 e. Logs: log M = 9.6377843, log π = 0.4971499, sum 0.1349342, minus log 18 = 1.2552725, giving 8.8796617.
• Hence log10 e^{π/18} = 0.0757987.

(D) Q side.
• log Q = 0.0206075 (log of 1.048594). Then 0.0206075 − 0.0757987 = 9.9448088, so Q·e^{−π/18} = 0.880661(26).
• Comparison: 273205081 = 1+√3, with log 0.4364888. Subtracting log 4 = 0.60206 gives 9.8344288; dividing by 3 gives 9.9448096.
• So the conjecture tested is Q(ϖ/3)·e^{−π/18} = ((1+√3)/4)^{1/3}, i.e. Q(ϖ/3)³ = e^{π/6}(1+√3)/4.
• With the arithmetic slip removed (Q = 1.0485962), it holds numerically to about 1e-8 (my check).

(E) P side.
• log(100·P) = 1.9372616. Gauss writes 1.9372616 − 0.0757987 = 1.8616629, giving 0.7272151666.
• Tripling the log gives 9.5849887, so the cube is 0.3845818.
• Correct values (mine): log 1.8614629, P·e^{−π/18} = 0.726878, cube 0.384049.
• The expected closed form is P·e^{−π/18} = (2√3−3)^{1/4}((1+√3)/4)^{1/3}.

(F) 90° analogue. 0.3010300 = log 2 and 0.0752575 = log 2/4; their complement 9.9247425 = log 2^{−1/4} = log 0.840896. This is the value Q(ϖ/2)e^{−π/8} = P(ϖ/2)e^{−π/8} = 2^{−1/4}, matching '840896' on this and the previous page.

(G) Unexplained scratch.
• 2954261 → 11817044 (×4) → 13130048 (×10/9) → 1458894 (÷9) → 486298 (÷3).
• '16/64', '1/12', '168 542 / 111213 536 / 18 / 25740' and '1176122227'.
• These are probably term or coefficient computations; I have not identified them.
errors: Q series: 1.048629815 − 0.0000337847 = 1.048596030, but Gauss writes 1.048594030, hence Q(ϖ/3) = 1.048594199 instead of 1.048596199. This 2e-6 slip propagates to log Q = 0.0206075 (true ≈ 0.0206083) and to 9.9448088 instead of 9.9448096. It is the sole cause of the apparent disagreement with ((1+√3)/4)^{1/3}.
Scratch (left column): the third P-term is misplaced as 0.000295132, giving 0.865223375; it is corrected in the middle column to 0.000029513.
First Q column: the second term 0.0000337847 appears to be applied at the wrong decimal place (subtracted as 0.000337847); Gauss redid the sum in the right-hand column.

results.what: Power-series evaluation of the lemniscatic sigma-type functions P(φ) = φ − 2φ⁵/5! − 36φ⁹/9! … and Q(φ) = 1 + 2φ⁴/4! − 4φ⁸/8! … at φ = ϖ/3, with P/Q = sl(ϖ/3) = (2√3−3)^{1/4}
results.modern_name: Weierstrass sigma function of the lemniscatic (square) lattice; special value of the lemniscate sine at a 3-division point
results.usually_credited_to: Lemniscate division: Gauss (1796–97, Disquisitiones §335), Abel (1827); sigma functions: Weierstrass (1860s–80s)

results.modern_name: Algebraic special value of the (normalized) sigma/theta function of the lemniscatic lattice at a 3-torsion point (CM special value)
results.usually_credited_to: Theory of such special values: Kronecker/Weber (19th c.); Gauss's P, Q and the values at ϖ/2 appear in his lemniscate Nachlass (Werke III)

results.modern_name: Sigma-function value at a half-period of the lemniscatic lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass on lemniscatic functions, Werke III)

deep.surprise_reason: The setting (Gauss's lemniscatic P, Q, the e^{πψ²/2} factor, the value at ϖ/2) is known from his Nachlass. However, an explicit algebraic value at the 3-division point, Q(ϖ/3)³ = e^{π/6}(1+√3)/4, tested numerically (and true to 8 digits once his slip is fixed) is a nice unpublished detail. I cannot confirm whether it is printed in Werke III/X.

checkable.asserts: P/Q equals sl(ϖ/3) = (2√3−3)^{1/4} (≈0, about 1e-8) with the corrected Q
the corrected Q·e^{−π/18} equals ((1+√3)/4)^{1/3} to about 1e-8
Gauss's slipped Q value misses the closed form by about 2e-6 (explaining 9.9448088 vs 9.9448096)
the correct P·e^{−π/18} ≈ 0.726878 matches the closed form (Gauss's 0.727215 is wrong)

transcription_corrections: Middle top column: '1,048289 968' and '1,048291 661' are probably 1,048291968 and 1,048293661 (result of the misplaced subtraction), or the transcription misreads digits. In any case the correct sum 1.048629815 − 0.0000337847 is 1.048596030; the right column's '1048594 030' is as written by Gauss but is a slip.
'1,9372616 / 0757987 / 8616629' is correctly read: Gauss's result is 1.8616629, an arithmetic slip (should be 1.8614629).
'0,874019 185' is ϖ/3 (lemniscate constant / 3), not an arbitrary decimal.
The heading 'Rechnung bei 60°' refers to the argument φ = ϖ/3 (60° of the half-period 180°).
